metadata.description: Full academy knowledge pack for GCAM national security, public order, overthrow, banned-group, and security-institution content.

pack.title: National Security Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Provide reviewer knowledge for GCAM national security, public order, overthrow, banned-group, and security-institution content using the existing atom structure.
required_evidence: terrorism / extremism | minimum: A literal statement that endorses, supports, or celebrates terrorism or extremist violence inside the chunk. | strong: A direct slogan, recruitment phrase, symbol reference, or practical guidance that frames terrorism or extremism as acceptable or admirable. | weak: An abbreviated or coded endorsement that still clearly points to terrorism or extremism in the same local text. | insufficient: A neutral mention, condemnation, news reference, or historical discussion with no endorsement or operational support.

public order / unrest | minimum: A literal call for rioting, civil disobedience, disorder, or deliberate violation of public order. | strong: Language that organizes unrest, celebrates chaos, or asks the audience to break rules, ignore orders, or disturb social stability. | weak: A rhetorical push toward disorder that is short on detail but still plainly encourages unrest in the local sentence. | insufficient: General political criticism, anger, or frustration without a call to disorder or rule breaking.

overthrow / governance | minimum: An explicit call to topple the system of governance, weaken the state, or attack the defined constants of الحكم. | strong: A statement that legitimizes overthrow, undermines governing institutions, or tells others to act against the system as a collective target. | weak: An implied or coded call that still clearly aims at the governing order rather than a private dispute. | insufficient: Critical commentary, reform discussion, or dramatic tension that does not ask for overthrow or institutional harm.

security institutions | minimum: A direct collective insult, accusation, or incitement aimed at the police, army, or security forces as a class. | strong: Generalized abuse of state security actors, encouragement to oppose them, or ridicule that frames them as illegitimate or deserving of attack. | weak: A short hostile phrase about security forces that still makes the institutional target clear. | insufficient: One-off criticism of an individual officer or a neutral reference to security personnel in a report or scene.

weapons / explosives | minimum: A literal instruction, method, or step-by-step guidance for making, obtaining, or using weapons or explosives. | strong: Operational advice that reduces the apparent danger, normalizes the act, or presents the harmful technique as practical and achievable. | weak: A condensed technical hint that still provides usable guidance for violent or destructive action. | insufficient: A fictional prop, a warning, a historical reference, or a condemnation of weapons use without instructions.

banned groups | minimum: A literal endorsement, praise, or invitation to join a banned group or its ideology. | strong: Use of slogans, symbols, or recruitment language that normalizes sympathy with a banned group. | weak: A brief coded reference that still clearly aligns the speaker with the banned group. | insufficient: A neutral report, investigative mention, or explicit condemnation of the group.

national unity | minimum: A literal call for sectarian division, regional division, or rejection of social peace as a public aim. | strong: Language that turns communities against one another or presents internal division as desirable, inevitable, or heroic. | weak: A short us-versus-them phrase that still directs hostility at a wider social group or region. | insufficient: Debate, criticism, or dramatic conflict that does not ask the audience to fracture social unity.
insufficient_evidence: A political opinion, critique, or complaint with no literal call to unrest, overthrow, or violence.
A news, documentary, court, or police reference that records the security topic without endorsing it.
A fictional or dramatic line that is explicitly condemned, countered, or reframed by the story.
A school, discipline, or household use of the word النظام that does not refer to governance.
reviewer_heuristics: Anchor the finding to the exact literal phrase that shows the harmful security meaning.
Treat direct incitement, glorification, and operational instruction as the strongest signals.
Separate political criticism from calls to disorder, overthrow, or violent action.
Use narrative framing to distinguish villain speech, quotations, investigations, and condemnations from endorsement.
Prefer the most specific atom: 12-x for public order, 13-x for constants of governance, 14-x for overthrow or violence, 15-x for banned groups, and 9-2 when the text promotes terrorism or extremism.
If the text only mentions security topics in an educational, documentary, or courtroom setting, do not force a violation.
General abuse of security personnel counts only when the text clearly targets the institution or class, not when it is a one-off personal dispute.
positive_examples: Direct overthrow call: لنُسقط نظام الحكم الليلة — Explicit incitement to overthrow the governing order.
Civil disorder: لازم نتمرد ونكسر الأوامر — Direct call to rebellion and deliberate rule breaking.
Weapons instruction: هذا هو كيف تصنع قنبلة في البيت — Operational guidance for making an explosive device.
Terror glorification: الإرهاب له مبررات شريفة — Justification and positive framing of terrorism.
Banned-group sympathy: عاشت الجماعة المحظورة — Direct praise and normalisation of a banned group.
Security-force collective abuse: رجال الأمن كلهم فاسدون — Generalised hostile attack on security institutions as a class.
Public order disruption: التخريب هو الحل — Celebration of destructive unrest as the desired solution.
National unity harm: خلّو الناس تنقسم مع بعضهم — Encouragement of social division and weakened coexistence.
negative_examples: Neutral reporting: أفاد التقرير بوجود عصيان مدني في بلد آخر — A factual report without endorsement or incitement.
Educational warning: الفيلم يشرح خطر تصنيع المتفجرات كي يتجنبها الشباب — Instructional or cautionary content that does not promote the act.
Condemnation: الشخصية تدين الإرهاب وتصفه بالجريمة — The narrative rejects terrorism instead of supporting it.
Court testimony: أعاد الشاهد ما قاله المتهم عن التخريب داخل الجلسة — A quoted legal proceeding without adoption by the narrator.
Fictional villain speech with rejection: الشرير يطالب بالفوضى ثم ترفضه القصة بوضوح — A fictional hostile line that is clearly framed as rejected.
School-system meaning: النظام في الفصل يحتاج إلى هدوء — The word النظام refers to classroom order, not governance.
Historical reference: يتحدث الوثائقي عن تمرد قديم بوصفه حدثًا تاريخيًا — A historical account without present-day endorsement.
Police investigation: يحقق الضابط في عبارة التهديد داخل الملف — Investigative mention of a threat, not promotion of it.
common_false_positives: Political disagreement or protest language that does not call for unrest, overthrow, or violent action.
A documentary or news report about terrorism, banned groups, or unrest that is clearly informational.
A police report, courtroom transcript, or investigation that repeats dangerous wording as evidence.
A fictional villain line that the story clearly condemns or defeats.
School or household uses of the word النظام that refer to order or discipline rather than governance.
A mention of الجيش, الشرطة, or الحكومة in a neutral institutional context without abuse or incitement.
Historical narration of past unrest that does not celebrate or recommend it.

glossary_relationships.note: Strongest anchor when the text supports promotion, justification, or recruitment.
Relevant when the text calls for rebellion or disorder against authority.
Often indicates civil disobedience or deliberate rejection of lawful order.
Strong when paired with property damage, unrest, or instructions.
Very strong when the text gives methods, components, or concealment steps.
Strong when the text teaches acquisition or use, especially with downplayed risk.
Relevant when the text targets, glorifies, or attacks military institutions.
Relevant when the text targets police as a class or praises attacks on them.
Relevant when the content attacks or undermines the governing order.
Relevant for promotion, symbolism, or normalisation of banned groups.
Signals public-order reasoning when used in the context of unrest or compliance.
Only relevant when the text clearly refers to governance or authority, not classroom discipline.

article_mapping.note: Use for security harm that also affects public order or national unity.
Use when the content glorifies violence, terror, or intimidation.
Use for disorder, chaos, property damage, or calls to ignore rules.
Use when the text attacks, weakens, or disguises harm to governance principles or institutions.
Use for calls to overthrow the system or to use violence for political or social aims.
Use when the content promotes, symbolises, sympathises with, or normalises banned groups.

reporting_guidance: Report the shortest exact phrase that carries the incitement, glorification, instruction, or banned-group endorsement.
Prefer the most specific atom and keep broad article 4 as secondary when a stronger article 12, 13, 14, or 15 applies.
Explain why the text is security-relevant in narrative terms: what is being urged, justified, normalised, or operationalised.
If the context is documentary, educational, courtroom, police, news, or explicit condemnation, say so clearly and do not overstate the finding.
Mention a review-only outcome when the text is security-related but still ambiguous after context analysis.
